newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end with losses as volume dwindles.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end with losses as volume dwindles.

text.p: Thinning volume accompanied a weaker Kuala Lumpur share market, where blue chips ended with moderate losses after an uninspired session.

News of a 773.4 million ringgit trade deficit in October failed to stir the market. "It's still way below the forecast (for all of 1996) given at the beginning of the year," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at Capitalcorp Securities.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised shares ended off 3.47 points to 1,193.83. Smaller stocks fared worse, losing 6.93 points or 1.29 percent to 530.01.
At day's end, 118 million shares changed hands, compared with 121.5 million on Monday. Losers trounced gainers by 441 to 146.
"I think we're correcting from a very overbought position in the Second Board," said Ralph Dixon, of TA Securities' international division. "Blue chips are holding reasonably well."

Nervousness about Wall Street's direction lingered in the background, dealers said. "Given the global uncertainties...the fact that our market is holding and volume is very thin shows there are no real sellers at this point," Moris said.
